title: Claude Code Commands
subtitle: 109 commands ship with Claude Code — this deck shows you the 20 that matter, and makes the other 89 safe to ignore.
footer: Twenty commands cover the whole job — the other eighty-nine are one /help away.

bands.heading: Steering the work
bands.deck: A control panel: what to do, which engine, how hard it thinks.

visual.explanation: Three independent levers: they set the order of work, the engine that runs it, and how deep each turn of reasoning goes.
visual.example: Enter /plan before the big refactor, then /effort xhigh for the security review pass.
visual.tradeoff: These steer the task; they never change the task itself.
visual.caption: What, who, and how hard — set independently.

bands.heading: Before you ship
bands.deck: Four lenses between you and a merge.

nodes.label: /diff
nodes.note: Interactive viewer of uncommitted changes and per-turn diffs

nodes.label: /security-review
nodes.note: Scans the branch diff for injection, auth, data exposure

nodes.label: /simplify
nodes.note: Four parallel review agents apply cleanup opportunities

evidence: /code-review high 1234 reviews PR #1234; /code-review --fix applies what it finds.
visual.explanation: Correctness, security, and cleanliness are three different questions asked of the same diff.
visual.tradeoff: Review costs minutes; an escape costs the release.
visual.caption: Three questions, one diff, no excuses.

callouts.label: /rewind

bands.heading: Act 2 — The full catalog, honestly sorted
bands.deck: The other 89 commands, four buckets — each in its place.

visual.explanation: Eighty-nine commands sort into four honest buckets; ignoring them is now deliberate.
visual.example: /cost aliases /usage; /vim is gone from the CLI.
visual.tradeoff: Without the sorting, all 109 look equally important.
visual.caption: Sorted so you can safely ignore most of it.

callouts.label: /loop
callouts.note: the scheduled family: recurring chores outside the loop

bands.heading: Worth knowing — eight that earn their place
bands.deck: Configuration and extension surfaces, one command each.

children.label: /config — opens Settings; accepts key=value pairs (theme, model, editor mode)
/hooks — views hook configurations for tool events
/mcp — manages MCP server connections and OAuth
/plugin — manages plugins with subcommands like list and install
/debug — enables session debug logging and reads the debug log
/help — shows all available commands; the catalog's own index
/skills — lists available skills with token counts
/verify — confirms a change works by building and running the app

bands.heading: Useful, but niche — nine for specific moments
bands.deck: Each shines exactly once in a while — and then it shines.

visual.explanation: Nine commands cluster around specific moments rather than roles, each exactly right when its moment arrives.
visual.example: /fork copies the thread into a background session.
visual.tradeoff: None is routine; timing the reach is the skill.
visual.caption: Know they exist; reach when the moment calls.

callouts.label: /help
callouts.note: the index every forgotten name resolves through

bands.heading: Aliases & the removed
bands.deck: Four aliases, three ghosts — know them so they never confuse you.

visual.explanation: Four names resolve twice; three names are gone from the CLI entirely.
visual.example: Typing /ultrareview routes to /code-review; typing /vim fails outright.
visual.tradeoff: Treating aliases as distinct commands doubles the catalog for nothing.
visual.caption: The catalog's history in one frame.
visual.axisX: Typed name still works ← → name is gone

callouts.label: /clear
callouts.note: fresh conversation between tasks; memory stays
